No moisture, contact pressure, isotropy, compression-response, aging, strength, expansion, fire/degradation or service-temperature law is inferred from these thermal experiments.

The Wet label in raw filenames denotes unconditioned samples kept indoors at 22 +/- 3 degC and relative humidity 40 +/- 20 percent. It does not mean water-saturated, nor does it supply exact sample moisture or zero moisture. These specimens are not assigned the source's separate oven-dried condition. The general conductivity method is ASTM C518 with through-thickness upward heat flow; the general capacity method is ASTM C1784-20 with equal-temperature plate steps. Applied contact pressure, calibrated instrument uncertainty, specimen-axis mapping and cross-property covariance are not provided. Conductivity and capacity are distinct runs; joint thermal use is conditional on treating the selected product/conditioning population as representative, not proof of identical coupons or independent measurements.

column5: The 3 complete native volume-capacity results are averaged at each source temperature. Temperatures round to 0.1 degC as in the primary reduction, giving 10,20,30,40 degC; conversion to kelvin adds exactly 273.15. Across-specimen sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)); it is retained as a discrete statistic, not a confidence interval or instrument uncertainty. Extra computed digits are arithmetic, not extra measurement resolution. Linear interpolation of mean C(T) is an authored local approximation to finite-step estimates; interpolation error is unquantified and extrapolation is disallowed.

The June 1 R1 file contains an aborted run and no final SI results table. It is excluded rather than treated as a zero, fourth independent specimen or repeat to average with the complete June 2 R1. The selected three complete June 2 specimens retain the measured capacity decrease near 30 degC and the larger scatter at 30 and 40 degC; no smoothing, monotonicity repair or implied measurement confidence is introduced.

No compatible density input is present for this source population. No bulk-density, reference-normalization-density or mass-specific heat claim is created. Native instrument volumetric heat capacity can drive volume-based thermal storage without estimating density.

column5: 3 specimens each provide three repeated cycles at each mean temperature: 9 readings per temperature, not 9 independent specimens. Raw measured mean temperatures round to 15,65 degC. The pooled arithmetic means 0.035976666666666664,0.045812222222222226 W/(m K) and sample SD 0.00012449899597988685,0.00015770048967725018 W/(m K) are explicit computations from the native rows; they are not claimed to be published site table values. These unrounded computed SD are separate descriptive statistics, not standard uncertainty. Linear interpolation between mean-temperature groups is an authored approximation with unquantified error. Only actual groups are retained; blank cells from aligned condition tables do not create measurements.

The thermal-conductivity curve requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. It explicitly substitutes the finite-gradient apparent HFM conductivity for a local scalar through-thickness coefficient at the same numerical temperature. This is an authored engineering approximation, not deconvolution of the 20 K plate difference, a point measurement or proof of isotropy. The apparent-thermal-conductivity curve retains its native test-mean-temperature axis.
